claim: In Gravesend a shop window is built from the street inward: a reveal, one sash pocket per bay with solid mullions between, a display box, then the shop; reveal, sashes and box share one floor and one ceiling, so the pane hung between a sash and the box carries no step band. The street-side record is two-sided to the reveal and carries the facade's lintel and stall riser at the facade's scale. A mullion must not reach the street face, where it would be a full-height slice of the facade's painted windows.
evidence: Gravesend, 2026-11-17 (projects/blood-city/experiments/shopfronts-streets/README.md): before, 24 of 24 glazed records also carried a step band; after, 0 of 20, and continuing collinear joins rose from 85% to 97% (tools/texture_continuity.py)
a blind reviewer: 'set into the wall: a recess, mullions or posts, a sill ledge and a dark frame' against 'laid flat on the wall' (projects/blood-city/experiments/shopfronts-streets/before-after.png)
the same helper served three venues built three ways (theatre, market hall, arcade)
use: glass.shopfront in blood-city gives the rectangles; bloodmap.glass.glaze(fit=True) keeps E6M1's glass density on a pane of any length; glass.recess_faults also accepts E6M1's own arrangement (pane between the recess and the shop, sill under the glass).
